H&F Bird Sightings

Expected arrivals and departures for Hammersmith & Fulham, alongside actual eBird hotspot sightings this month.

What this board shows

The monthly Arrivals and Departures tables show birds expected to move into or out of Hammersmith & Fulham at this time of year. They sit alongside actual eBird observations submitted at borough hotspots during the selected month.

Seasonal windows describe typical movement. A hotspot report confirms a submitted observation at a place and date; by itself, it does not prove a first arrival, departure or local breeding.

Data sources & method

Expected movements: seasonal timing and likely origins or destinations are based on BTO BirdTrack patterns and BTO BirdFacts. Local context is informed by the Wormwood Scrubs 2024/25 ecological monitoring report. Country names are examples of likely destinations or origins, not tracked routes.

BirdWeather detections: public BirdNET audio detections from listening stations whose coordinates fall inside the borough boundary. They are automated sound identifications, not human-verified sightings or individual-bird counts; confidence is a model score, not confirmation.

Actual sightings: valid reports from eBird hotspots and other mapped locations within Hammersmith & Fulham are refreshed daily. Nearby reports come from eBird’s recent geospatial feed, which returns recent records (the latest observation per species in its search area); coordinates are clipped to the borough boundary and private locations are omitted. The nearby feed supplements the hotspot checklist feed, which retains multiple reports per hotspot. These records are evidence of reports, not proof of first arrival, departure or local breeding.

Hotspot map: markers show public eBird hotspot locations inside the borough; private mapped locations are not plotted. Background map tiles are provided by OpenStreetMap and load from its servers when the map is opened. Species names link to the RSPB A–Z search.

Historical species list: the NBN Atlas list uses a borough-confirmed occurrence export from 2016–2025. NBN coverage is incomplete, so it is used only to show species recorded in the area, not to predict monthly movements. Occurrence totals count records, not individual birds; a missing record does not prove absence.

Show the bird board on a TV

The site can prepare a full-screen display, but the browser controls casting to your TV.

  1. On a Samsung phone, swipe down twice and tap Smart View or Cast, then select your TV.
  2. On a computer with Chrome, open the ⋮ menu, choose Cast, then select your TV and cast this tab.

Make sure your phone or computer and TV are on the same Wi‑Fi network.

Contributor species boards

Each board lists the species reported by one publicly named eBird checklist observer in the selected month. Names are the public display names returned by eBird; the board does not show email or contact details. Nearby mapped-location records are excluded; counted-bird totals appear only where eBird supplies them.
